regulators.name: Reserve Bank of India
regulators.stance_note: No general practice of publishing comments received on discussion papers. Commenters self-publish instead (NASSCOM posted its own submission on the Charges paper; Vidhi posted its 2019 PA/PG submission). Individual comment-archives exist only because commenters chose to publish. RTI is the fallback route.

regulators.name: Securities and Exchange Board of India
regulators.stance_note: Posts consultation papers and the comments received on its public-comments portal; a board-approved procedure (18 Dec 2024) formalised pre-legislative consultation for regulation-making.

regulators.name: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
regulators.stance_note: Consultation papers published on its portal. In June 2026 IRDAI proposed a formal regulation-making framework: minimum 21-day public comment window and a general statement of response to comments published by the date regulations are notified. Until notified, publication of comments is not a settled practice.

regulators.name: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
regulators.stance_note: Runs a Public Comments section; its discussion papers instruct commenters to submit through the website with stakeholder categories, and comments are published there.

regulators.name: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
regulators.stance_note: Consultation papers published on the site (e.g. Sept 2025 valuation-alignment paper via PIB). Whether comments received are published is unverified — flagged for checking.

regulators.name: International Financial Services Centres Authority
regulators.stance_note: Consultation papers listed on ifsca.gov.in. Whether comments received are published is unverified — flagged for checking.

consultations.title: Discussion Paper on Charges in Payment Systems (40 questions on UPI/IMPS/NEFT/card charges)
consultations.outcome_note: Submissions were never published by RBI; commenters self-published (NASSCOM's full submission is public by its own choice). The paper set off the UPI-charges debate; the finance ministry publicly denied any plan to charge UPI, and the merchant-discount-rate question resurfaced in later rule-making.

consultations.title: Discussion Paper on Guidelines for Payment Gateways and Payment Aggregators
consultations.outcome_note: Final PA/PG directions followed in 2020; the comment record survives only because commenters like Vidhi published their own submissions, including its delegated-legislation objections on the PSS Act.

consultations.title: Consultation Paper on Review of Closing Auction Session, Market Timings and Settlement Methodologies for Derivative Contracts
consultations.outcome_note: SEBI's verified account reported 20,000 comments by 19:00 IST on the final submission day, 3 Oct 2026. Submissions and the regulator's response remain to be tracked.

consultations.title: Consultation Paper on Corporate Governance: secretarial compliance, auditors, related-party transactions
SEBI (Procedure for Making, Amending and Reviewing of Regulations) — formalised pre-legislative consultation
consultations.outcome_note: Board-approved procedure (18 Dec 2024) making structured pre-legislative consultation mandatory — the strongest transparency baseline among the six desks; the watch compares other regulators against it.

consultations.title: Public Consultation Paper on Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution (commissions, EoM, Bima Sugam, Public Insurance Registry)
consultations.outcome_note: Live watch: who comments on distribution economics (insurers, banks-as-banca partners, brokers, web aggregators) and whether IRDAI publishes a response statement when the final rules land.

consultations.title: Draft framework for regulation-making and public consultation under the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act 2025
consultations.outcome_note: If notified as proposed: minimum 21-day comment windows, and a published general statement of response to comments by notification date — plus a fresh consultation round when final rules differ substantially from drafts.

consultations.title: Discussion Paper: amendments to CIRP, Liquidation and Personal Guarantor Regulations
consultations.outcome_note: Comments submitted through the IBBI website's Public Comments section.

consultations.title: Discussion Paper: Guidance to Insolvency Professionals for Due Diligence to Identify Fraudulent or Malicious Initiation of Corporate Insolvency
Consultation Paper to Align Valuation Practices in the NPS Architecture
consultations.outcome_note: Released with an invitation for stakeholder comments; PFRDA's comment-publication practice is the open question this register tracks.

interests.name: Payments Council of India
interests.role: Apex payments-industry council formed in 2013 under the aegis of IAMAI; self-describes as representing 90%+ of the payments industry; runs committees (merchant aggregators & acquirers, payment processors, networks) and publishes policy-position pages on regulation.

interests.name: Internet and Mobile Association of India
interests.role: Industry body for internet and mobile businesses; parent under whose aegis PCI was formed; files consultation responses and policy positions across digital payments and platform regulation.

interests.name: NASSCOM
interests.role: IT-industry body; self-published its feedback on RBI's Charges-in-Payment-Systems discussion paper (Oct 2022), arguing that zero or low fees can deter innovation and competition — a documented position on the UPI pricing question.

interests.name: Indian Banks' Association
interests.role: Association of banks and the banking interest; engages regulators on banking rules; standard commenter on RBI consultation papers.

interests.name: FICCI
interests.role: Industry chamber; files consultation responses across financial-sector regulation through committees and task forces.

interests.name: Confederation of Indian Industry
interests.role: Industry chamber; files consultation responses across financial-sector regulation through committees and task forces.

interests.name: ASSOCHAM
interests.role: Industry chamber; files consultation responses across financial-sector regulation through committees and task forces.

interests.name: US-India Strategic Partnership Forum
interests.role: US business forum advocating for member companies in India including financial services; engages on fintech and digital-economy policy with Indian regulators and government.

interests.name: iSPIRT Foundation
interests.role: Non-profit software think tank behind India Stack advocacy; registered in UFF's member roster (SROTrac). A policy NGO with an unusual seat at the table: builds and pitches the infrastructure the state then regulates.

interests.name: Digital India Foundation
interests.role: Policy foundation working on digital-economy issues incl. payments and platform regulation; files submissions and op-eds in regulatory debates.

interests.name: Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy
interests.role: Independent legal-policy think tank; self-published its submission to RBI's 2019 payment-gateways/aggregators discussion paper — including the delegated-legislation argument on the PSS Act. One of the few commenters whose RBI consultation position is public by its own choice.

interests.name: Dvara Research
interests.role: Research institution focused on financial-systems design for low-income households; publishes on customer-protection architecture in payments and credit.

interests.name: CUTS International
interests.role: Consumer-interest NGO (Consumer Unity & Trust Society) that files comments in financial-sector consultations from the user's side of the table.

interests.name: Finance Industry Development Council
interests.role: RBI-recognised SRO for NBFCs; per SROTrac's tracking the most active consultation respondent among the recognised SROs. Roster and governance tracked at SROTrac.

interests.name: Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment
interests.role: RBI-recognised fintech SRO (Aug 2024); responds to digital-lending consultations. Roster and governance tracked at SROTrac.

interests.name: Unified Fintech Forum
interests.role: RBI-recognised fintech SRO (Sep 2026; born as DLAI); its member roster is the who's-who of fintech policy interest. Tracked at SROTrac.

interests.name: Sahamati
interests.role: RBI-recognised SRO for the account-aggregator ecosystem; chaired since 2025 by former RBI Deputy Governor R. Gandhi — a documented revolving-door row (see Doors).

interests.name: Microfinance Institutions Network
interests.role: RBI-recognised SRO for NBFC-MFIs (2014); H.R. Khan (former RBI DG) was appointed first chairman of the Code for Responsible Lending steering committee in micro-credit — see Doors.

interests.name: Sa-Dhan
interests.role: RBI-recognised SRO (2015) for community-development finance institutions. Tracked at SROTrac.

interests.name: Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India
interests.role: RBI-recognised SRO (Jan 2026) of authorised forex dealers; writes its own market rulebook. Tracked at SROTrac.

interests.name: Self-Regulated PSO Association
interests.role: RBI-recognised SRO (Nov 2025) of payment system operators founded by practitioners. Tracked at SROTrac.

doors.appointer_note: Appointed by RBI itself for two years
doors.why_consumer_care: The central bank placed its own former deputy governor on a private bank's board — the same bank it would supersede and rescue within a year.

doors.appointer_note: RBI approval letter dated 1 Sep 2025
doors.why_consumer_care: Successive terms on a regulated bank's board long after leaving the regulator — with the approval of the regulator itself; the appointment shows why cooling-off disclosure rules matter for banking supervision.

doors.appointer_note: Sahamati board; now also RBI-recognised SRO (see SROTrac)
doors.why_consumer_care: The alliance that writes account-aggregator standards is now chaired by an ex-RBI deputy governor — a rule-borrower led by a rule-writer; track both layers together.

doors.appointer_note: Company board
doors.why_consumer_care: Market-infrastructure vendor chaired by a former deputy governor; demonstrates how post-retirement board seats cluster in regulated financial-market plumbing.

doors.former_office: Deputy Governor (2011–2016); earlier RBI nominee on the Bandhan board
doors.appointer_note: Bank board
doors.why_consumer_care: A deputy governor who sat as RBI's nominee on a bank during its licence era returned to chair that same bank after retiring.

doors.new_role: Non-executive (part-time) Chairman from 30 Jan 2024; independent director from Dec 2021
doors.appointer_note: Bank board
doors.why_consumer_care: Second regulated bank chaired by the same ex-deputy governor — the pattern, not the person, is the watch item.

doors.new_role: First chairman, steering committee of the Code for Responsible Lending (CRL) in micro-credit
doors.appointer_note: Industry committee
doors.why_consumer_care: The micro-credit industry's self-regulatory code body is chaired by an ex-RBI deputy governor — the SROTrac layer borrowing a regulator's prestige; consumer redress depends on that code working.

doors.appointer_note: Company board
doors.why_consumer_care: India's markets watchdog chairman joined a large listed group's board a year after leaving SEBI — the classic securities-regulator revolving door.

doors.new_org: Nippon Life India Asset Management Ltd
doors.appointer_note: Company board
doors.why_consumer_care: The former markets regulator now chairs the board of a mutual-fund house SEBI regulates directly.

doors.new_role: Independent Director and non-executive Chairperson (two years from 27 Mar 2023)
doors.appointer_note: Company board
doors.why_consumer_care: Board seat in a listed media group — disclosure filings are the public record; tracked here because every door move for a regulator head belongs in one ledger.

doors.appointer_note: Company board
doors.why_consumer_care: Listed-healthcare board seat; part of the same post-SEBI portfolio that includes regulated mutual-fund and listed-entity roles.

doors.appointer_note: Company board
doors.why_consumer_care: Services-sector listed company adds a former regulator head to its board.

doors.appointer_note: Board elevated him from independent director (since 2018) to non-executive chairman on 12 Aug 2020
doors.why_consumer_care: As RBI DG he supervised NBFCs and housing-finance lenders; he then chaired an NBFC whose loan practices sat inside that supervision

doors.appointer_note: Board seat announced 30 May 2025, 17 days after PayU received its final RBI payment-aggregator licence (13 May 2025); also on BSE, Airtel Payments Bank and Havells boards
doors.why_consumer_care: A licensed payment aggregator hired the former banking supervisor weeks after getting its licence — supervision and supervised meet at the same table

doors.appointer_note: Assumed charge 2 Jan 2015 for a three-year term; chaired the bank's audit, customer-service and fraud-monitoring committees per AGM notices
doors.why_consumer_care: The RBI's senior-most woman regulator, who handled payments and forex, became chair of India's largest private bank and of its fraud-monitoring committee

doors.appointer_note: Announced 16–17 Jun 2025; IIFL Finance is an RBI-regulated retail NBFC
doors.why_consumer_care: The deputy governor who oversaw currency management and NBFC policy joined an NBFC board five years after retirement

doors.appointer_note: Independent director on Axis board from 30 May 2023; part-time chairman effective 27 Oct 2023; RBI approval for a second term (27 Oct 2026–26 Oct 2029) reported Sep 2026; also EY India adviser and Razorpay advisory-board chair
doors.why_consumer_care: The deputy governor who led banking supervision chairs a supervised bank — and got a second term, making the door a corridor

doors.new_org: Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC — NBFC SRO)
doors.appointer_note: FIDC, the RBI-recognised SRO for NBFCs, announced his induction (alongside Bajaj Finance vice-chairman Rajeev Jain) on 16 Sep 2026; welcome event 17 Sep
doors.why_consumer_care: A former banking regulator joining the SRO layer collapses the stack: the rule-borrowers' own trade body now carries a former rule-writer

doors.former_org: Securities and Exchange Board of India
doors.appointer_note: Five-year term effective 26 May 2020; KFin is a SEBI-regulated registrar and transfer agent for mutual funds and listed companies; he also directs Ascent Fund Services (Singapore) and Hexagram Fintech
doors.why_consumer_care: SEBI's member for market intermediaries joined a SEBI-regulated market intermediary — the same desk at a different address

doors.new_role: Independent Director (30 Apr 2016 - 29 Apr 2026, term ended)
doors.appointer_note: Sanofi India board/AGM; appointment dated 30 Apr 2016 per the company's own annual reports (the company website's 2017 date conflicts with its own ARs and MCA records)
doors.why_consumer_care: Post-RBI, the former bank regulator ended up chairing the company that computes the benchmarks Indian loans and bonds price off

doors.former_office: Chairperson, IRDAI (2022–2025); earlier Financial Services Secretary
doors.former_org: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
doors.new_role: Non-executive (part-time) chairman and independent director, 3-year term
doors.appointer_note: RBI prior-approval letter dated 22 Apr 2026; board approved 25 Jun 2026; effective 5 Jul 2026, succeeding founder-chairman Anup Kumar Sinha — the second former regulator to chair Bandhan after H.R. Khan
doors.why_consumer_care: Bandhan has now hired two former RBI/IRDAI chiefs as chairmen in seven years; the revolving door is becoming a hiring pipeline

doors.former_org: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
doors.appointer_note: Appointed amid a board exodus; he also sat on the CEO search committee that selected Rana Kapoor's successor. Yes Bank was placed under RBI reconstruction in March 2020
doors.why_consumer_care: The former insurance regulator sat on Yes Bank's board through its final crisis; depositors paid for the governance failure he was hired to guard against

doors.appointer_note: BSE board elected him chairman on 17 May 2022 from among public interest directors (PI director since Jan 2018); appointment subject to SEBI approval.
doors.why_consumer_care: India’s largest exchange by listed companies — the body whose listing framework governs every company a retail investor can buy — is chaired by an ex-RBI deputy governor, with his former co-regulator signing off on the chair.

doors.former_org: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
doors.appointer_note: Jana SFB board appointment announced 28 Oct 2021, months after his IRDAI term ended May 2021; part-time chairman subject to RBI approval.
doors.why_consumer_care: The insurance regulator’s chief became chairman of a deposit-taking small finance bank within months of demitting office — the same small-finance segment IRDAI-adjacent distribution and bancassurance rules touch.

doors.appointer_note: BharatPe board appointment announced 13 Sep 2022 alongside a governance overhaul under chairman Rajnish Kumar (ex-SBI chairman).
doors.why_consumer_care: The payments fintech that went through a public governance crisis hired the ex-RBI deputy governor who once oversaw payment systems; whether the promised governance reform holds is directly a merchant-and-consumer question.

doors.appointer_note: Board meeting of 9 Feb 2023 appointed him additional director (non-executive, independent) and chairman, five-year term w.e.f. 9 Feb 2023; recorded in the company’s AGM notice of 14 Jul 2023.
doors.why_consumer_care: Within two years of leaving the RBI the career central banker chairs an IRDAI-regulated life insurer; policyholders get an experienced chair, but the braid of ex-regulators across insurance boards is exactly what this ledger exists to track.

doors.appointer_note: Reappointment by CRISIL board commencing 10 Jul 2025, subject to shareholder approval; she earlier chaired HDFC Bank (see 2015 row).
doors.why_consumer_care: Credit ratings steer where retail money parks in debt funds and NCDs; an ex-RBI deputy governor on the board of a SEBI-regulated rating agency keeps the regulator-rater relationship in view.

doors.former_org: Securities and Exchange Board of India
doors.appointer_note: PRISM board announcement of 25 Feb 2026 as the company prepares for an IPO.
doors.why_consumer_care: An IPO-bound company stocks its board with the ex-SEBI chairman while SEBI will process that very listing — the door swinging toward the gatekeeper is the textbook case this register watches.

doors.former_office: Whole Time Member, SEBI (2016–2021); earlier Executive Director, RBI
doors.former_org: Securities and Exchange Board of India
doors.appointer_note: Reappointment effective 21 Nov 2025, subject to shareholder approval; per the appointment note he also chairs SEBI’s advisory committees on secondary markets and the corporate bond market.
doors.why_consumer_care: A SEBI-regulated credit-rating agency seats an ex-SEBI whole-time member who simultaneously chairs SEBI advisory committees — disclosed and legal, but the same desk writes guidance the rater lives under.

doors.former_office: Whole Time Member, SEBI (2016–2021); earlier Executive Director, RBI
doors.former_org: Securities and Exchange Board of India
doors.appointer_note: Six-month reappointment effective 29 Jan 2026 (originally appointed 2022); LIC’s official bio page also lists directorships at City Union Bank, India International Bullion Exchange IFSC, DSP Pension Fund Managers and CARE Ratings.
doors.why_consumer_care: India’s largest insurer keeps an ex-market regulator on its board while he holds parallel seats at a bank, a bullion exchange and a pension fund manager — a cluster worth watching across four regulators’ jurisdictions.

doors.former_office: Whole Time Member, SEBI (2022–2025); earlier Managing Director, SBI
doors.former_org: Securities and Exchange Board of India
doors.appointer_note: Board resolution by circulation dated 1 Jun 2026, five-year term; the door also ran in reverse — SBI MD before SEBI.
doors.why_consumer_care: A SEBI whole-time member joins the board of India’s second-largest private bank within twelve months of leaving the regulator — the reverse door (banker to regulator) and the forward door (regulator to bank) in one career.

doors.appointer_note: Elevated from independent director (joined Jun 2025, see kanungo-iifl-2025) to non-executive chairman at the 19 Dec 2025 board meeting, with immediate effect.
doors.why_consumer_care: RBI had barred IIFL’s gold-loan business in Mar 2025 over supervisory concerns (ban lifted after remediation); the NBFC answered by making an ex-RBI deputy governor its chairman.
